proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(x_0\in U\) and put \(r:=\operatorname{rank}Da(x_0)\).  The conclusion is immediate if \(r\leq k\), so suppose for contradiction that \(r>k\).  By the definition of matrix rank, there are \(r\) domain coordinates and \(r\) response coordinates for which the corresponding \(r\times r\) minor of \(Da(x_0)\) is nonsingular.  Let \(\iota:W\to U\) be the affine coordinate inclusion from an open neighborhood \(W\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) of the selected coordinates of \(x_0\), with all other coordinates fixed at their values at \(x_0\), and let \(\pi:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R^r\) be the selected response projection.  Then
\[
F:=\pi\circ a\circ\iota:W\longrightarrow\mathbb R^r
\]
is \(C^1\), and \(DF\) is nonsingular at the point corresponding to \(x_0\).  By \(\texttt{lem:inverse-function-theorem}\), after shrinking \(W\) to a nonempty open neighborhood \(W_0\), the map \(F|_{W_0}\) is injective.

Set \(b_0:=b\circ\iota|_{W_0}\).  If \(b_0(z)=b_0(z')\), the hypothesis of the lemma gives \(a(\iota(z))=a(\iota(z'))\), and hence \(F(z)=F(z')\).  Injectivity of \(F|_{W_0}\) yields \(z=z'\).  Thus \(b_0:W_0\to\mathbb R^k\) is a continuous injection.  Because \(r>k\), the map
\[
\widetilde b_0:W_0\longrightarrow\mathbb R^r,
\qquad
\widetilde b_0(z):=(b_0(z),0_{r-k}),
\]
is also continuous and injective.  By \(\texttt{lem:invariance-of-domain}\), its image is open in \(\mathbb R^r\).  On the other hand, that image lies in the proper coordinate subspace \(\mathbb R^k\times\{0\}^{r-k}\), whose interior in \(\mathbb R^r\) is empty.  This contradiction shows \(r\leq k\).  Since \(x_0\) was arbitrary, \(\operatorname{rank}Da(x)\leq k\) for every \(x\in U\).

Fix disjoint measured sets \(A,B\subseteq V_0\), and let \(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_t\) be the asserted vertex-disjoint collider-free paths, with distinct endpoints \(a_i\in A\) and \(b_i\in B\).  Because arrows in the layered graph point downward and measured vertices have no children, each \(\pi_i\) is a trek: it has a unique highest vertex, and its two directed arms run from that vertex to \(a_i\) and \(b_i\).

We first show that the rank constraint \(\operatorname{rank}D\mathbb E[X_B\mid X_A=\cdot]\leq t-1\) is not graph-forced.  Construct a linear Gaussian structural equation model on \(G\) with mutually independent centered Gaussian disturbances of variance one.  Give coefficient one to every edge on the paths \(\pi_i\), and initially give coefficient zero to every other edge.  Vertex-disjointness makes the active components containing the \(\pi_i\) disjoint.  Consequently the \(t\times t\) covariance submatrix with rows \((b_1,\ldots,b_t)\) and columns \((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\) is diagonal, and its \(i\)-th diagonal entry is the strictly positive variance contribution propagated from the highest vertex of \(\pi_i\).  It therefore has nonzero determinant.

Every measured coordinate has its own independent variance-one disturbance, so \(\Sigma_{AA}:=\operatorname{Cov}(X_A,X_A)\) is positive definite.  For completeness, with \(\Sigma_{BA}:=\operatorname{Cov}(X_B,X_A)\), define
\[
W:=X_B-\Sigma_{BA}\Sigma_{AA}^{-1}X_A.
\]
The vector \((W,X_A)\) is jointly Gaussian and has zero cross-covariance.  Its joint characteristic function therefore factors into the product of its two marginal characteristic functions, so \(W\) and \(X_A\) are independent.  Hence
\[
\mathbb E[X_B\mid X_A=x]
=\Sigma_{BA}\Sigma_{AA}^{-1}x,
\qquad
\operatorname{rank}D\mathbb E[X_B\mid X_A=x]
=\operatorname{rank}\Sigma_{BA}\geq t. \tag{1}
\]
If the graph convention requires every displayed arrow to have a nonzero structural coefficient, replace each zero coefficient by a sufficiently small nonzero number.  The selected covariance determinant is a continuous polynomial function of the coefficients and is nonzero at the displayed point, so it remains nonzero after a sufficiently small perturbation.  Independent positive-variance Gaussian disturbances give a nondegenerate differentiable member of the published structural family, and Gaussian conditional laws are determined by smooth conditional means and conditioning-independent conditional covariance.  Thus the perturbed witness obeys the differentiability and conditional-sufficiency restrictions of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}}\).

The generalized rank-faithfulness hypothesis is now used in its stated graph-entailment direction: a Jacobian rank inequality for the actual law may hold only when it is forced throughout the structural model on \(G\).  Equation (1) supplies a member of that model for which the inequality \(\operatorname{rank}<t\) fails.  Therefore the actual law cannot satisfy that inequality.  Since \((A,B)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), every admissible \(C^1\) conditional-mean representative has the same essential-supremum rank, and the definition of \(R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}\) gives
\[
R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}(A,B)\geq t.
\]
This uses rank faithfulness only for the particular queried minor witnessed by the private paths, not a blanket equality between rank and minimum separator size.

For \(v\in V_\ell\), let \(\mathcal U_\ell(v)\) be the union of \(v\) and all vertices on the retained pure-child chains generated by the recursion defining \(D_\ell(v)\).  We prove by induction on \(\ell\) that the sets \(\mathcal U_\ell(v)\), \(v\in V_\ell\), are pairwise disjoint rooted trees, that their leaves are exactly \(D_\ell(v)\), and that every nonroot vertex of such a tree has exactly one parent in the full graph.

For \(\ell=0\), \(\mathcal U_0(v)=D_0(v)=\{v\}\), so the claim is immediate.  Suppose it holds at level \(\ell\), and let \(h\in V_{\ell+1}\).  By definition,
\[
D_{\ell+1}(h)=\bigcup_{v\in B_h}D_\ell(v),
\qquad
B_h=\{v\in V_\ell:\operatorname{Pa}_G(v)=\{h\}\}.
\]
Each \(v\in B_h\) has exactly the one parent \(h\).  Distinct blocks \(B_h\) are disjoint, and the induction hypothesis makes the trees below their members disjoint.  Adjoining the edges \(h\to v\), \(v\in B_h\), therefore gives a rooted tree and proves disjointness at level \(\ell+1\).  The two-pure-child assumption also gives \(|B_h|\geq2\), so every retained tree is nonempty; recursively, \(|D_\ell(v)|\geq2^\ell\).

We next establish the claimed cuts directly from the definition of an active path.  Below height \(\ell\), an edge entering a nonroot vertex of \(\mathcal U_\ell(v)\) must be the unique pure-parent edge already in that tree.  A path from a retained source leaf that leaves its retained tree without passing upward through its root must instead follow an arrow from a tree vertex down to an excluded child.  A wholly descending continuation cannot enter another retained tree, because entry into any nonroot vertex of that tree would be a second parent edge, contrary to purity.  Thus, to reach a retained leaf in another tree, the path must later reverse vertical direction.  At its first reversal, the two incident arrows both point into the reversal vertex, so that vertex is a collider.  The conditioning sets under consideration lie at height at least \(\ell\), and hence contain neither that collider nor any of its lower descendants.  Such a path is blocked.  It follows that every active path from \(D_\ell(A)\) to a different retained tree must first pass through a source root in \(A\) and then, if it continues upward, through a member of \(\operatorname{Pa}_G(A)\).

Consequently, when \(\ell\geq1\), conditioning on the latent source roots \(A\subseteq V_\ell\) blocks every such path.  If \(C\subseteq V_{\ell+1}\) contains \(\operatorname{Pa}_G(a)\) for every \(a\in A\), every path that exits upward is blocked at its first parent in \(C\), while the preceding collider argument blocks every downward exit.  Thus \(C\) \(d\)-separates the source surrogate trees from the other retained trees.  If a source root \(v\) is parentless, there is no upward exit at all, so \(D_\ell(v)\) and the other retained trees are \(d\)-separated by the empty set.  These are precisely the restricted cuts stated in the lemma; conditioning on extra vertices in \(C\) cannot reopen an already blocked source exit because the first conditioned parent is a noncollider on that exit.

Finally, consider a current-layer fork \(u\leftarrow h\to v\).  Choose any \(x\in D_\ell(u)\) and \(y\in D_\ell(v)\).  Concatenating the unique retained directed chains gives
\[
x\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow u\leftarrow h\to v\to\cdots\to y.
\]
Every internal vertex on this path has at most one incident arrowhead along the path, so the path is collider-free.  If the current forks are vertex-disjoint, their roots, endpoints, and retained trees are disjoint by the first part of the proof; the lifted measured paths are therefore vertex-disjoint.  This proves every assertion.

Fix \(v\in V_\ell\) and abbreviate \(A:=D_\ell(v)\) and \(B:=D_\ell(V_\ell\setminus\{v\})\).  Suppose first that \(\operatorname{Pa}_G(v)=\varnothing\).  By \(\texttt{lem:pure-surrogate-cuts}\), the empty set \(d\)-separates \(A\) and \(B\).  The directed global Markov property gives \(X_A\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}X_B\).  Hence the constant map \(x\mapsto\mathbb E[X_B]\) is a continuously differentiable version of \(\mathbb E[X_B\mid X_A=x]\), with derivative rank zero.  The queried pair is in \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), so the definition of the version-invariant oracle forces every admissible version to have the same essential-supremum rank.  Therefore
\[
\rho_\ell(\{v\},V_\ell\setminus\{v\})
=R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}(A,B)=0. \tag{1}
\]
If the response is empty, the same equality follows from the stipulated empty-endpoint convention.

Conversely, suppose \(h\in\operatorname{Pa}_G(v)\).  The two-pure-child assumption supplies a pure child \(b\in B_h\) distinct from \(v\): if \(v\notin B_h\), choose any member of \(B_h\), and if \(v\in B_h\), choose another member.  Then \(b\in V_\ell\setminus\{v\}\), and the fork \(v\leftarrow h\to b\) lifts by \(\texttt{lem:pure-surrogate-cuts}\) to a collider-free measured path between \(A\) and \(B\).  Applying \(\texttt{lem:private-path-lower}\) with \(t=1\) gives
\[
\rho_\ell(\{v\},V_\ell\setminus\{v\})
=R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}(A,B)\geq1. \tag{2}
\]
Equations (1) and (2) prove the equivalence.  In particular, parentless vertices are detected without the separator-rank regularity repair needed by the pair and neutrality upper bounds.

Let \(X\) be jointly Gaussian with nonsingular covariance matrix \(\Sigma\).  For any nonempty measured predictor set \(A\), the principal submatrix \(\Sigma_{AA}\) is positive definite.  With \(\Sigma_{BA}:=\operatorname{Cov}(X_B,X_A)\), the residual
\[
W:=X_B-\mathbb E[X_B]-\Sigma_{BA}\Sigma_{AA}^{-1}(X_A-\mathbb E[X_A])
\]
is jointly Gaussian with \(X_A\) and has zero cross-covariance with \(X_A\).  Factorization of the joint Gaussian characteristic function gives \(W\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}X_A\), and therefore
\[
\mathbb E[X_B\mid X_A=x]
=\mathbb E[X_B]+\Sigma_{BA}\Sigma_{AA}^{-1}(x-\mathbb E[X_A]),
\qquad
J_{A,B}=\Sigma_{BA}\Sigma_{AA}^{-1}. \tag{1}
\]
Because \(X_A\) has a strictly positive density on \(\mathbb R^{|A|}\), two continuous versions that agree \(P_{X_A}\)-almost surely agree everywhere: otherwise continuity would give a nonempty open ball of disagreement, and that ball has positive probability.  Applying this argument to their coordinatewise differences and then differentiating the everywhere equality shows that all \(C^1\) versions have derivative (1).  Thus every nonempty RankPeel pair belongs to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\); empty pairs do so by definition.  Since right multiplication by the invertible matrix \(\Sigma_{AA}^{-1}\) preserves rank,
\[
R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}(A,B)=\operatorname{rank}J_{A,B}
=\operatorname{rank}\Sigma_{BA}. \tag{2}
\]

If a latent set \(Z\) \(d\)-separates the two endpoint sets, the directed global Markov property gives \(X_A\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}X_B\mid Z\).  Gaussian linear projection supplies an affine version \(\mathbb E[X_B\mid Z]=\alpha+\Lambda Z\), and conditional independence plus iterated expectation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E[X_B\mid X_A=x]
&=\mathbb E\!\left[\mathbb E[X_B\mid Z,X_A]\mid X_A=x\right]\\
&=\mathbb E\!\left[\mathbb E[X_B\mid Z]\mid X_A=x\right]\\
&=\alpha+\Lambda\,\mathbb E[Z\mid X_A=x].
\end{aligned} \tag{3}
\]
The last conditional mean is affine in \(x\), so differentiating (3) shows that the derivative in (1) factors through \(\mathbb R^{|Z|}\) and has rank at most \(|Z|\), together with the elementary bounds \(|A|\) and \(|B|\).  Conversely, the private-path construction in \(\texttt{lem:private-path-lower}\) is itself linear Gaussian and exhibits a nonzero queried minor; generalized rank faithfulness excludes its cancellation for the actual member.  Thus the query-specific upper and lower arguments become exactly Gaussian cross-covariance rank separation and generic noncancellation, as claimed.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open, let \(F:U\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable, and suppose \(DF(x_0)\) is invertible at \(x_0\in U\). Then there are open neighborhoods \(U_0\ni x_0\) and \(V_0\ni F(x_0)\) such that \(F|_{U_0}:U_0\to V_0\) is a continuously differentiable bijection with continuously differentiable inverse.

attestation.note: The stated local diffeomorphism form is the conclusion of Theorem 9.24 in the cited third edition; the bibliography key and stable edition record are supplied here.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \((G,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}}\) satisfying the query-local first-jet-determining and fibre-coherence hypotheses, consider a measured endpoint pair \((D_\ell(A),D_\ell(B))\) issued by \(\operatorname{RankPeel}\) as a singleton, pair, baseline-neutrality, or augmented-neutrality query.  That pair belongs to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\).  If a latent set \(Z\subseteq V\setminus V_0\) is one of the restricted separators used for this query, then
\[
R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}(D_\ell(A),D_\ell(B))
\leq\min\{|D_\ell(A)|,|D_\ell(B)|,|Z|\}.
\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The published conditional-sufficiency condition is only an almost-sure statement about conditional versions and does not ensure pointwise fibre coherence on the open domain; the published-class boundary witness in \(\texttt{thm:analytic-boundary-characterization}\) also violates first-jet determinacy. The replacement is therefore restricted to the query-local first-jet-determining, fibre-coherent subclass, which is a strict subclass of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}}\), and it does not assume the desired rank inequality itself.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For a member of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}}\) satisfying the query-local first-jet-determining and fibre-coherence hypotheses, and for distinct current vertices \(u,v\in V_\ell\) with nonempty parent sets,
\[
\rho_\ell(\{u,v\},V_\ell\setminus\{u,v\})\leq1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{Pa}_G(u)=\operatorname{Pa}_G(v)=\{h\}
\]
for some \(h\in V_{\ell+1}\).  Every such pair query is in \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\).  Consequently the nontrivial connected components of \(\sim_\ell\) are exactly the pure blocks \(B_h\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The same-parent implication uses the restricted separator upper bound and hence requires the query-local version repair. Conditions 1--3 alone do not supply it; the replacement is on the strict first-jet-determining, fibre-coherent subclass of the published class, while the different-parent private-path lower bound is unchanged.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \((G,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}}\) satisfy the query-local first-jet-determining and fibre-coherence hypotheses.  Let \(H=V_{\ell+1}\), choose any \(s_h\in B_h\), let \(c\in V_\ell\) be nonparentless and outside every pure block, and take \(C\subseteq H\) with \(k=|C|\).  The baseline and augmented measured endpoint pairs belong to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), and
\[
\rho_\ell(S_C,T_C(c))=k,
\qquad
\rho_\ell(S_C\cup\{c\},T_C(c))=
\begin{cases}
k,&\operatorname{Pa}_G(c)\subseteq C,\\
k+1,&\operatorname{Pa}_G(c)\nsubseteq C.
\end{cases}
\]
Hence \(N_c(C)=1\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Pa}_G(c)\subseteq C\), independently of the representative choices.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Both exact upper bounds in the \(k\)-versus-\(k+1\) comparison use restricted latent separators. The unchanged published Conditions 1--3 neither determine derivatives across all conditional-mean versions nor impose the required pointwise fibre coherence. The replacement is on the strict query-local first-jet-determining, fibre-coherent subclass; it does not assume any rank conclusion or saturated-rank property.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Theorem 1 (RankPeel reconstruction on the query-regular strict subclass).  For every \((G,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}}\) satisfying the query-local first-jet-determining and fibre-coherence hypotheses, \(\operatorname{RankPeel}(P_X,R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X})\) completes and returns \(\widehat G\) with \([\widehat G]=\theta_G\).  It recovers the full binary adjacency matrix, up to independent within-layer permutations of latent labels, by deterministic pairwise pure-block tests and representative-neutrality deletion over measured pure-descendant surrogates.  The strict-subclass restriction is necessary for this law-invariant oracle construction: on the unchanged published class there is a member for which RankPeel reaches an unstable pair and returns \(\bot\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The explicit one-latent four-measurement counterexample in \(\texttt{thm:analytic-boundary-characterization}\) makes an unchanged-class law-invariant reconstruction theorem false: RankPeel reaches an unstable pair and returns \(\bot\). The replacement is an exact recovery theorem only on the strict query-local first-jet-determining, fibre-coherent subclass of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}}\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Theorem 2 (Quadratic oracle complexity).  If \(|V_0|=p\), \(\operatorname{RankPeel}\) returns either \(\bot\) or a graph after at most \(p^2+p\) membership-and-rank calls to the law-invariant oracle, \(O(p^3)\) elementary bookkeeping, \(O(p^2)\) graph storage, and at most \(1+\lfloor\log_2p\rfloor\) nonempty iterations.  On the query-local first-jet-determining, fibre-coherent strict subclass in Theorem 1, the run is complete and the returned graph is the identified adjacency target.  The polynomial bound is an algorithmic comparison with the exhaustive subset construction, not an unchanged-class strict-tightening claim.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The execution bound remains valid for every run, but its recovery interpretation cannot be advertised as an unchanged-class strict tightening because the published-class counterexample can force \(\bot\). The replacement restricts only the recovery clause to the strict query-regular subclass and leaves the unconditional call and bookkeeping bounds intact.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Corollary 1 (Oracle-relative replay record).  Every complete RankPeel run emits a transcript \(\mathcal T\) of \(O(p^3+p^2\log p)\) bits for which \(\operatorname{Verify}(P_X,R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X},\mathcal T,\widehat G)=1\).  Replaying it uses at most \(p^2+p\) law-invariant oracle calls and \(O(p^3)\) bookkeeping.  If \((G,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}}\) also satisfies the query-local first-jet-determining and fibre-coherence hypotheses, every accepted canonical replay records a graph representing \(\theta_G\); outside that strict subclass, acceptance certifies only faithful replay relative to the supplied oracle.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Deterministic oracle replay is unconditional, whereas identification soundness depends on the repaired reconstruction theorem. The replacement restricts only the conclusion that the recorded graph represents \(\theta_G\) to the strict first-jet-determining, fibre-coherent subclass and explicitly leaves replay outside it oracle-relative.

proposed_assumptions.condition:
For every predictor set \(A\subseteq V_0\) occurring in a measured endpoint pair adaptively requested by \(\operatorname{RankPeel}(P_X,R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X})\), there is a common open neighborhood \(\mathcal U_A\supseteq\operatorname{supp}(P_{X_A})\) such that, for every \(h\in C^1(\mathcal U_A;\mathbb R)\),
\[
h(X_A)=0\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
Dh(X_A)=0\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\]
proposed_assumptions.reason: This condition is exactly the query-local first-order support property that makes derivatives of all \(C^1\) conditional-mean versions agree almost surely. It is necessary for a law-invariant oracle on supports such as those excluded by the published-class counterexample.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This is not the combinatorial RankPeel crux: it is the explicit support/version regularity boundary needed to make the oracle well defined, and it does not assert any separator rank or reconstruction conclusion.

proposed_assumptions.condition:
For every measured endpoint pair \((A,B)\) adaptively requested by \(\operatorname{RankPeel}(P_X,R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X})\), and for every latent set \(Z\subseteq V\setminus V_0\) used as a \(d\)-separator for that query in the parentless, pure-block, or neutrality argument, there exist a common open neighborhood \(\mathcal U_A\supseteq\operatorname{supp}(P_{X_A})\), a representative \(f^0\in\mathfrak F_{A,B}(P_X)\), and a map \(g\in C^1(\mathcal U_A;\mathbb R^{|Z|})\) such that
\[
g(x)=g(x')\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f^0(x)=f^0(x')
\qquad\text{for all }x,x'\in\mathcal U_A.
\]
proposed_assumptions.reason: The published almost-sure conditional-sufficiency statement does not by itself select an off-support conditional-mean version that is constant on the sufficient-map fibres. This query- and separator-local condition supplies exactly that set-theoretic factorization, without calling it observable and without requiring a differentiable outer map.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This is an explicit analytic subclass restriction rather than the new graph-combinatorial kernel: it supplies only the fibre premise used by the topological rank bound and does not assume the bound, the \(k\)-versus-\(k+1\) identity, or recovery.

open_obligations.partial_result:
Conditional on application of the two proposed query-regularity hypotheses, the exact \(k\)-versus-\(k+1\) argument is complete.  For each \(h\in C\), choose \(b_h\in B_h\setminus\{s_h\}\).  Since \(c\) lies outside every pure block, all \(b_h\) belong to \(T_C(c)\), and the \(k\) forks
\[
s_h\leftarrow h\to b_h,\qquad h\in C,
\]
are vertex-disjoint.  The private-path lower lemma gives \(\rho_\ell(S_C,T_C(c))\geq k\), while \(C\) is a restricted separator for this baseline query, so the regularized separator lemma gives the reverse inequality.  Thus the baseline rank is exactly \(k\).

If \(\operatorname{Pa}_G(c)\subseteq C\), the same forks give augmented rank at least \(k\), and \(C\) contains the parents of every source root in \(S_C\cup\{c\}\); the restricted separator upper bound gives augmented rank at most \(k\).  If instead \(q\in\operatorname{Pa}_G(c)\setminus C\), choose \(b_q\in B_q\).  Then \(b_q\in T_C(c)\), and
\[
\{s_h\leftarrow h\to b_h:h\in C\}
\cup\{c\leftarrow q\to b_q\}
\]
is a family of \(k+1\) vertex-disjoint forks.  The private-path lemma yields augmented rank at least \(k+1\).  At \(\ell=0\), the predictor dimension gives the upper bound \(k+1\).  At \(\ell\geq1\), the \(k+1\) latent source roots \(S_C\cup\{c\}\) form the restricted separator supplied by the pure-surrogate lemma, and the regularized separator lemma again gives the upper bound \(k+1\).  The argument uses only block membership, so it is unchanged for any choices \(s_h\in B_h\).  Consequently the equality predicate holds exactly when \(\operatorname{Pa}_G(c)\subseteq C\), and sequential deletion removes every nonparent and no parent, in any order.

prose_updates.tldr: Prashant, Ng, Zhang, and Huang identify the full binary adjacency matrix of their nonlinear latent hierarchy and reuse measured pure descendants as higher-layer surrogates. RankPeel gives a deterministic pairwise-block and representative-deletion protocol with at most \(p^2+p\) observed rank queries, \(O(p^3)\) bookkeeping, and an oracle-relative replay record. An explicit smooth one-latent four-measurement member of the unchanged published class has two admissible conditional-mean versions with different Jacobian ranks, so full-class law-invariant recovery is false. Exact RankPeel recovery is therefore claimed only on the strict query-local first-jet-determining, fibre-coherent subclass; fibre coherence is latent and separator-relative, not observable. The parentless test, private-path lower bound, pure-surrogate cuts, and topological bottleneck are proved independently, while the regularized separator, pairwise, neutrality, reconstruction, recovery-complexity, and replay-soundness claims await application of the two explicit hypotheses.

project_justification.gap: The closest nonlinear result already identifies the complete binary adjacency matrix and uses measured pure descendants recursively, but its construction exhaustively searches subset families and gives no explicit polynomial observed-query budget. Moreover, its Conditions 1--3 do not make conditional-mean Jacobian rank invariant across all smooth versions: the retained published-class boundary example reaches a RankPeel pair with ranks one and two under two valid extensions.
project_justification.niche: On the strict subclass where every adaptive predictor support is first-jet determining and every restricted latent separator admits a fibre-coherent conditional-mean representative, the same graph target can be approached by deterministic pairwise block discovery and monotone parent deletion. The fibre-coherence restriction is a latent, query-specific analytic hypothesis rather than an observable test.
project_justification.fill: The repaired contribution is a conditional recovery certificate: graph-specific pure-surrogate cuts and private paths combine with a topological bottleneck to yield the exact rank decisions once the two query-regularity hypotheses hold. RankPeel then has a quadratic oracle-call budget and a replayable transcript. This is an algorithmic result on a strict subclass, not an unchanged-class strengthening of the published identification theorem.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The analysis is at the population-oracle level and excludes the cost of evaluating or estimating conditional-mean Jacobian ranks. On the strict query-local first-jet-determining, fibre-coherent subclass, every requested rank is version-stable and supports the recovery theorem; on the unchanged published class RankPeel may return \(\bot\). No finite-sample Jacobian estimator, rank-test calibration, or image-data consistency result is asserted.

Their result informs RankPeel, but the two promises are not matched after the analytic boundary result: RankPeel's law-invariant recovery theorem is restricted to a query-local first-jet-determining, fibre-coherent strict subclass, while its unconditional contribution is only the deterministic oracle protocol and execution bound. Huang, Low, Xie, Glymour, and Zhang motivate the pure-descendant surrogate motif in a linear IL\(^{2}\)H model, with different covariance-rank assumptions and a Markov-equivalence target. prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The graph-side early-kill analysis found no surrogate-cut counterexample in the prescribed \(676\) three-level configurations, but finite enumeration is not a proof; the recursive pure-surrogate lemma supplies the proof. The analytic obstruction is decisive: the unchanged published Conditions 1--3 allow a smooth boundary member whose conditional-mean Jacobian rank depends on the chosen \(C^1\) version. The repaired results therefore require query-local first-jet determinacy and latent separator fibre coherence. These conditions are not claimed observable, and no blanket separator-equals-rank identity, saturated-rank assumption, or faithfulness inheritance after latent contraction is used.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The structural target remains the full binary adjacency matrix modulo independent within-layer latent relabeling. The unchanged Prashant--Ng--Zhang--Huang class is not law-invariantly recovered by RankPeel: the explicit one-latent four-measurement counterexample can force an unstable pair and \(\bot\). Exact recovery, its recovery interpretation in the complexity theorem, and graph soundness of replay are limited to the strict query-local first-jet-determining, fibre-coherent subclass. Fibre coherence refers to latent separators and is not observable. For arbitrary oracle inputs, only termination, the \(p^2+p\) call bound, bookkeeping bounds, and deterministic replay are claimed. The note does not provide polynomial-time oracle evaluation, nonparametric Jacobian estimation, finite-sample recovery, or practical CelebA consistency.
